
### Definition for the notes of the Unit 3 - Regular and Non-Regular Grammars in the subject of Theory of Automata and Formal Languages

* Regular Grammars: These are grammars in which the set of strings that can be generated by the grammar can be recognized by a finite automaton.

* Non-Regular Grammars: These are grammars in which the set of strings that can be generated by the grammar cannot be recognized by a finite automaton. Examples of non-regular grammars include context-sensitive and unrestricted grammars.
